items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: I had a quartet which included Ray Nance on cornet with me.

ctx.x: Tell me about working with your own group. How did the musical scene change for you over the years? I mean you’ve always managed to find work. But has there been a number of years, or a decade, where things have been tougher?

Oh yeah, sure. Places I worked for years no longer existed, Monk. Restaurants out of business. Night clubs out of business. I mean like we’re talking about Eddie Condon’s, they folded up when they moved from the Village. They were in the Village, they moved Uptown to this certain hotel, 56th Street. It was after a couple of years or so and then they went out of business. Nick’s went out of business. The Metropole went out of business. I was at The Gaslight Club for ten years with my quartet. Eventually they went…
When did it become let’s say acceptable to mix racially in the groups in New York City? Was there ever a problem for you?
